1046085596173815809.a: Years ago I set a corporate policy of no admin rights on PCs. This meant people had to get every app approved. I was a monster! Then someone tried corporate espionage on a low level claims handler. Security policy isolated the issue to one user without access to secrets, the end.

1046085597864087552.a: Critical parts of the virus/worm crashed and failed assuming it had free reign. This kind of attack is meant to hit someone ignorant just doing their job. That infection escalates itself to admin on the local PC and tries to jump to other machines which trust it via the network.

1046085604935684097.a: My point is, entire departments of execs wanted exceptions when they were the most exposed. Of course then you must ask why someone is afraid of their work computer being audited and admin locked... This lack of security was pervasive in corporations, prolly still is.

1046085606315560965.a: So when an outsider is so upset at what they see you doing with things like insurance or health data that they feel the need to show you, after likely just telling you over and over, then be thankful and not vindictive. Your own IT staff has likely been thinking or saying it too.
